description: Large multi-stemmed tree in natural habitat (seepy rich spicebush wetland). Maybe an escape, or else planted for some reason?? (there is a hiking trail nearby). ID made using the 1965 Flora of Japan. Key features are the dimorphic tepals (see small slender tepals in 2nd image) and a small leaf subtending the flower (not clear in images), which distinguish it from M. stellata (and others).  Reportedly naturalized on mainland Korea, so not impossible that it could find its way into the landscape from ornamental individuals.
